_note: ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO INPUT — the numbers below are synthetic placeholders for testing the pipeline, not real results.
keywords: cryptocurrency; Bitcoin; deep learning; LSTM; variational mode decomposition; forecasting
problem: Bitcoin prices are highly volatile and non-stationary, which degrades single-model forecasters. Investors and risk managers need accurate multi-horizon forecasts.
research_questions: RQ1: Does decomposing the price series with VMD before LSTM forecasting reduce error compared with ARIMA and a plain LSTM? RQ2: Is the improvement statistically significant (Diebold-Mariano test)?
contributions: 1) A VMD-LSTM hybrid for daily Bitcoin closing prices. 2) A comparison with ARIMA and LSTM on 1-day and 7-day horizons. 3) Statistical significance testing of forecast accuracy differences.
method: Daily close prices are decomposed by variational mode decomposition (VMD) into K=5 intrinsic modes. Each mode is forecast by a separate LSTM (2 layers, 64 units, look-back 30 days, Adam optimizer, learning rate 0.001, early stopping). Mode forecasts are summed to obtain the price forecast. Baselines: ARIMA (order selected by AIC) and a single LSTM on raw prices.
data_description: Daily BTC-USD closing prices, 2018-01-01 to 2024-12-31 (2557 observations). Chronological split 80/20 (train/test). Min-max scaling fitted on training data only.
experimental_setup: Metrics: RMSE, MAE, MAPE on the test set (inverse-scaled prices, USD). Horizons: 1 day and 7 days ahead (direct strategy). Five runs with different random seeds; mean reported. Diebold-Mariano test with squared-error loss.
ablations: Number of modes K: K=3 RMSE 1236.8; K=5 RMSE 1104.6; K=7 RMSE 1129.5 (horizon 1).
discussion_notes: Decomposition separates the low-frequency trend from high-frequency noise; errors grow with horizon for all models.
limitations: Single asset; no exogenous variables; transaction costs not considered.
